guide.summary: Gaudí landmarks, the cathedral, Picasso and Catalan art museums, a market, tapas bars, seafront rice, a cocktail bar, a pastry shop and specialty coffee, each checked against its own website.
guide.tip: Park Güell tickets must be bought in advance online and hold for 30 minutes after your slot, while Museu Picasso and MNAC publish no Monday opening, so put the museums on other days.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Museu Picasso lists hours only Tuesday to Sunday, and MNAC is closed on Mondays except public holidays. El Xampanyet is closed on Sundays and opens only in the evening on Mondays.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Park Güell tickets must be bought in advance and online, and entry is allowed up to 30 minutes after your slot. Palau de la Música Catalana tours cost €2 more at the box office than online.

toolkit.label: Walk-in only
toolkit.copy: Paradiso takes no advance reservations and runs a virtual queue you join by scanning a QR code at the door. El Xampanyet also states that it does not accept reservations.

toolkit.label: Free and late
toolkit.copy: MNAC is free on Saturdays from 3pm and the first Sunday of the month, with an advance online reservation. Casa Batlló is open every day until 10:30pm, and La Pedrera runs night visits.

guide.dek: Book Gaudí sites and Park Güell before you fly, then leave mornings for coffee and the old town and evenings for walk-in tapas and cocktails.
intro: You can build a first Barcelona trip around Gaudí. Sagrada Família is open in October from 9am to 7pm on weekdays, 9am to 6pm on Saturdays and 10:30am to 7pm on Sundays, with shorter hours from November to February. Individual visitors enter on the Nativity façade, on Carrer de la Marina. Park Güell sells tickets online and in advance only, for visits between 9:30am and 7:30pm, and your entry holds for 30 minutes after the time on your ticket.

On Passeig de Gràcia, Casa Batlló opens every day from 9am to 10:30pm. Its 2026 programme includes Magical Nights concerts and the exhibition Gaudí-Miró-Gomis: Deconstructed. Further up the avenue, La Pedrera-Casa Milà keeps summer hours of 9am to 8:30pm until 1 November 2026, then 9am to 6:30pm from 2 November. It closes on 25 December 2026 and from 11 to 17 January 2027, and its rooftop shuts when it rains.

In the old town, Barcelona Cathedral receives tourist visits on weekdays from 9:30am to 6:30pm, and only from 2pm to 5pm on Sundays. Museu Picasso on Carrer de Montcada opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 7pm, in winter, and its exhibition Picasso and Architecture runs from 20 November 2026 to 7 March 2027. On Montjuïc, MNAC is free on Saturdays from 3pm and on the first Sunday of each month if you reserve online. Palau de la Música Catalana runs 50-minute guided tours between 9am and 3:30pm.

For food, El Xampanyet on Carrer de Montcada takes no reservations and closes on Sundays. Can Fisher, on Bogatell beach, serves Ebro Delta rice dishes daily from 12:30pm to midnight. Disfrutar takes bookings online. Paradiso, ranked 17th on the World's 50 Best Bars 2026 list, works through a QR-code virtual queue rather than bookings. For mornings, Petit Nomad now opens seven days a week, Federal Café in the Gòtic serves daily from 9am to 4:30pm, and Hofmann's Born shop sells pastries every day.
summaryCards: Pair a booked Sagrada Família slot with an online-only Park Güell ticket, then walk Passeig de Gràcia for Casa Batlló and La Pedrera.
Start with coffee at Petit Nomad or Hidden Coffee Roasters in El Born, then visit Museu Picasso on Carrer de Montcada, which opens at 10am Tuesday to Sunday in winter.
Book Park Güell and the Palau de la Música tour online, but plan to walk in or queue for El Xampanyet and Paradiso, which take no reservations.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. La Boqueria's official site returned nothing readable, Fundació Joan Miró's site refused automated reading (403) and Brunells' site refused the connection, so they are not included. Bohl, Tapeo, Two Schmucks and Baluard had no reachable official website. Quimet & Quimet and Dr Stravinsky published an address but no hours or current content. Several places were only partly published: Disfrutar and Paradiso show no opening hours, the Aquarium's closing times did not load, Park Güell gives entrances but no street number, MNAC's current exhibitions are undated, and Three Marks Coffee lists two conflicting sets of hours for Ausiàs Marc. The Sagrada Família site also shows an undated notice that the Gaudí House Museum is temporarily closed. This guide has fewer than the 25-place target because of these gaps.
